description: A browser game where students run a Moon or Mars base for 360 days and learn the engineering trade-offs that decide whether a mission succeeds or fails.
summary: A browser game where students run a Moon or Mars base for 360 days and learn the engineering trade-offs that decide whether a mission succeeds or fails.
details:
Outpost One puts students aged 10–15 in charge of a 4-person base on the Moon or Mars. Each turn covers 15 days. Players spend Build Points on solar arrays, energy storage, a fission reactor, life support, greenhouses, regolith shielding and a storm shelter. Then they use sliders to share a limited power supply between heating, life support, food, mining and science.

The trade-offs are real. On the Moon, solar power drops to zero during the 14-day lunar night, so players must store energy or build a reactor. On Mars, sunlight is weaker, dust storms cut solar power to 35%, and no supply rockets come. Radiation builds up quietly unless the habitat is shielded early. Every kilowatt spent on science is taken from safety.

A live forecast shows what each choice will do before the turn is played. Events like solar flares, dust storms, plant disease and breakdowns are each based on a real mission. When the mission ends, a debrief shows charts and explains what went right or wrong, so students can try again with a better plan.
